benchmark.category: a Telegram deal-reposting system that reads Flipkart deal channels and reposts them to destination channels with converted affiliate links
benchmark.users: a deal-channel operator running @dealfetch and Deltfetch who needs to see from the admin panel whether the reader is running, what it logged and how long each post takes

requirements.statement: The Channel Reader tab on /admin shows the reader's enabled state, connected state, Telegram user, source channels, the sender of the last post (spare account or the bot's name), last read time, last sent time with the seconds it took and last error; the connection cell reads 'No Telegram login saved — log in first' when the reader is enabled and no Telegram login is stored, 'Switched off' when the reader is disabled, and the connected user when a session is stored; no cell is left empty or shown as connected when the stored state is missing, and the tab's helper text says reader posts appear in Converter History labelled 'Reader: source → channel'
requirements.notes: Amended for the three connection states the build now renders (no login saved / switched off / connected) and for the pointer to where reader logs are visible. The user's new line is exactly 'check still reader not connected', so a generic disconnected cell fails the intent; the preview runs with reader_enabled true and no Telegram session, which is precisely the no-login wording to see.

requirements.statement: GET /api/public/reader/status returns enabled, connected, has_login (whether a Telegram user session is stored for this site), user, sources[], poster (the spare account or the bot name that sent the last post), last_read, last_sent with the measured duration in milliseconds and last_error with the stored values; it sets last_error to where 'login' with a message saying no Telegram login is saved on this site when the reader is enabled and no session is stored, and returns null or an explicit never for a timestamp that has not happened yet
requirements.notes: Amended for the status contract the build now exposes: has_login plus a structured where/message last_error. The user asks why the reader is still not connected, so the status must name the missing login instead of only connected false. The preview deliberately has no Telegram session, and that state must be reported honestly, never faked as connected.

requirements.source_phrase: kindly you check the website https://dealloot.onrender.com/admin
requirements.statement: The admin panel at the app's public /admin route (https://dealloot.onrender.com/admin) serves the password form to a visitor with no session and, after signing in with RadheKrishna@#12, renders the admin tabs and the Channel Reader status with the real stored values rather than a blank page, a build error or an error page
requirements.notes: The user names the host and password and asks the agent to check that site; the deployed build must behave as the preview does. The build context says the app had not yet been deployed or run on Render, so this is the first thing that can be reported missing.

requirements.statement: The Channel Reader tab answers 'is it working' in one visible line derived from the stored state: it shows the reader as working only when the reader is enabled, a Telegram login is saved and the last cycle completed, and otherwise names the blocking reason (switched off, no Telegram login saved, or the last error message), never showing working while the status reports has_login false or an unresolved error
requirements.notes: The user's new line asks whether the system is working now; a panel that only lists raw fields leaves the question unanswered. The verdict must be computed from the stored status fields, so an app that prints 'working' while no Telegram login is saved fails.

requirements.statement: Under 'Last post sent' the Channel Reader tab shows a per-step timing breakdown for the last post — Telegram delivery, opening the short link, conversion, posting and the app's own part — with each step's duration in seconds that do not exceed the total shown for that post, a dash for a step that did not run, and numbers that change when a new post is sent
requirements.notes: The user asks where the timing is visible; the build adds the breakdown under 'Last post sent'. Each displayed value must equal the stored value, so a static sample breakdown is the failure to catch.

requirements.statement: The reader stores with each post the durations of its steps (delivery, link opening, conversion, posting, own overhead) and the total, and GET /api/public/reader/status returns the breakdown for the last sent post unchanged from what was stored, with null for a step that did not run, and a failed post records the steps it completed
requirements.notes: Build description: the new timing line breaks the post into Telegram delivery, opening the link, conversion, posting and our own part; it exists so the 2 s target can be judged, and only a stored per-post record survives a reload.

requirements.source_phrase: where i can see all the logs
requirements.statement: The Converter History tab shows every reader post as its own row labelled 'Reader: <source channel> → <destination channel>' with the product, the converted link, the time and that post's elapsed seconds, distinguishes those rows from manual conversions, and shows an explicit empty message when the reader has not posted yet
requirements.notes: The user asks where the logs are; the build answers 'Reader posts appear in Converter History'. A row that omits the source or destination channel leaves the operator unable to trace a post.

requirements.statement: The conversion history endpoint returns for each row its origin (reader or manual), the source channel, the destination channel, the product code, the converted link, the created timestamp and the elapsed milliseconds for reader rows, returns the same rows after a reload and in a new admin session, and returns an empty list when nothing has been converted
requirements.notes: Build description: reader posts are written into Converter History. Origin, source and destination must be stored with the row, not guessed by the screen, so the log survives a reload and can be filtered.

requirements.statement: When Telegram refuses a login code request, the error returned to the admin panel names the cause: SEND_CODE_UNAVAILABLE, PHONE_NUMBER_BANNED and FLOOD each map to their own message and any other refusal carries Telegram's own code in the form '(Telegram said: CODE)', so a refusal is never shown as a generic failure or as a success
requirements.notes: Build description names the loginError mapping in src/server/sankmo-bot.server.ts; it exists because the user kept asking whether the system works and could not tell a banned number from a flood wait. Code review of that mapper only: do not press Send code and do not call POST /sankmo-bot/send-code, since it would send a real Telegram code.
